# A directive is a command a dependency's author wrote, and completing a module
# runs it on this machine unread. So a module outside the org runs nothing until
# its own go.mod asks with a //go:gendep line.

env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod

# The module carries a directive and no opt-in line. The fetch says so, and the
# file its generator writes is not in the module directory.
go mod download example.com/generatedunasked
stderr 'example.com/generatedunasked@v1.0.0 is outside github.com/wow-look-at-my/'
stderr '//go:gendep'
! exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generatedunasked@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# The package is what the zip published, so the build fails at the symbol the
# generator would have declared rather than at a missing file.
! go build ./...
stderr 'lang.Name'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.16

require example.com/generatedunasked v1.0.0
-- use.go --
package use

import "example.com/generatedunasked/lang"

var Name = lang.Name()
